subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — proposed claim-response runbook & defense-control checklist
messages:
From: Sophia Tran <sophia.tran@helixcloud.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@helixcloud.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form indemnity - proposed scope + evidence timeline

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is HelixCloud’s draft redline to the MSA/order form focusing on the indemnity sections. High level ask: HelixCloud needs a reasonably broad customer indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to our customers’ data and configurations.

Key asks in the redline:
- Notice window: 10 business days for initial notice
- Evidence: we will need a listed package (samples, logs, prompted prompt bundles) and a single point-of-contact for evidence requests
- Defense control: HelixCloud prefers to retain defense for third-party patent assertions unless Redwood elects to take over and show proof of indemnity coverage

We expect to go to procurement on Monday and would like a proposed operational runbook from Redwood that explains: what evidence you can provide (format and retention), expected timelines for a technical response, and a named technical liaison for the claim.

I attached the redline PDF (HelixCloud_Draft_MSA_Redline.pdf). Can your legal and ops teams propose a narrow evidence schema and a defense-control compromise we can take to our counsel?

Thanks,
Sophia
Senior Contracts Manager
HelixCloud

Attachment: HelixCloud_Draft_MSA_Redline.pdf (application/pdf)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Sophia Tran <sophia.tran@helixcloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity - proposed scope + evidence timeline

Sophia —

Appreciate the redline. Quick read shows two practical paths that would make procurement comfortable while keeping operational burden bounded:

1) Narrowed coverage: Redwood accepts indemnity for direct infringement claims arising from model outputs (i.e., where output includes a claim of pre-existing third-party patented content), but excludes claims arising solely from customer-provided data, unless customer requests fine-tuning or shared models that introduce third-party content.

2) Joint evidence playbook: We’ll provide a standardized evidence package (logs, prompting bundle snapshot, model hash, request timestamps) delivered via a secure S3 link; retention for six months by default with options to extend for higher-tier customers.

Operationally we can commit to:
- A named technical liaison (Jordan Blake) for evidence triage
- Initial triage within 3 business days of receiving notice + prioritized technical report within 7 business days
- A single zip package with the fields Helix listed; we’ll draft a template (see attached RI_evidence_template.xlsx)

On defense control: Redwood is comfortable offering a defense-control compromise — Helix can lead the initial response and Redwood reserves the right to step in if Helix declines to defend within 5 business days or if Redwood reasonably believes Helix’s defense would prejudice Redwood’s rights. That compromise preserves practical control while giving Helix runway to coordinate with counsel.

If that sounds workable I’ll loop in Kimberly (legal) for language and get a short runbook back to you by Monday.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI_evidence_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Sophia Tran <sophia.tran@helixcloud.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2027 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity - proposed scope + evidence timeline

Marcus / Sophia —

I reviewed Marcus’s operational proposal and Helix’s redline. Below are specific legal suggestions to convert the proposal into contract language. I’m keeping the changes pragmatic to avoid procurement stalls.

Suggested contract bullets (high level):
- Trigger: indemnity limited to third-party claims that allege Redwood’s model output infringes a third party’s patent or copyright (exclude claims that arise solely from customer-supplied content unless customer explicitly requested model fine-tuning with that content).
- Notice & cooperation: 10 business days notice is acceptable; Redwood’s cooperation obligations limited to providing technical evidence and logs as reasonably requested (we’ll enumerate required fields in the playbook).
- Defense control: adopt Marcus’s compromise but add an explicit step: if Helix commences defense, Redwood may participate (with counsel) and preserve subrogation rights; if Helix refuses or does not reasonably defend within 5 business days after Redwood’s offer to assume defense, Redwood may assume defense.
- Cap: propose standard order-form cap (e.g., greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $500k) — ask procurement if Helix has a preferred cap formula.

Operational asks of Helix (to include in runbook):
- Provide SOC 2 Type II report (or host SOC link) and a named procurement contact for evidentiary communications
- Accept Redwood’s evidence template as the baseline; any additional items must be requested at the outset to avoid iterative evidence requests

I’ve attached a draft runbook doc (Redwood_Response_Playbook_v1.docx) which includes evidence field definitions and the triage timeline. Marcus, Jordan — please review the triage SLA in section 2 and confirm Jordan can commit to the 3/7 business-day windows.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Response_Playbook_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Sophia Tran <sophia.tran@helixcloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: John Patel <john.patel@helixcloud.com>, HelixCloud Legal <legal@helixcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity - proposed scope + evidence timeline

Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turn. The runbook looks reasonable and the evidence template is helpful. A few clarifications from Helix legal:
- Defense control carve: we can accept the step-in language as long as there’s an explicit ‘no prejudice’ clause clarifying that Redwood’s defense cannot limit Helix’s rights to recover from the claimant later.
- Retention: Helix usually requires 12 months of evidence retention for paid customers; can Redwood confirm if that’s available for enterprise customers (we’ll accept six months for self-serve tiers).
- E-discovery: Helix counsel wants a short joint e-discovery statement we can include in the runbook about how to securely exchange evidence; can Redwood propose 2–3 bullet points?

I’m copying our counsel and John Patel (procurement). If we can get a confirmed SLA matrix + joint e-discovery bullets and the defense carve clarified, procurement is ready to move forward.

Sophia Tran
Senior Contracts Manager
HelixCloud

Forwarded attachments: HelixCloud_Draft_MSA_Redline.pdf

Sophia / team —

This works. Finalizing action items and owners below so procurement has a single view:

- Redwood ops (Jordan): confirm evidence retention tiers (6 months default, 12 months enterprise) and sign off on 3/7 business-day triage SLA by EOD Tuesday.
- Redwood (Marcus): draft 3 e-discovery bullets for the runbook (encrypted transfer, minimal necessary fields, audit trail) and post to DocSend.
- Helix (Sophia / John): confirm preferred cap formula (flat $ cap vs. multiple of prior 12 months spend) and confirm acceptance of retention tiers.

Meeting: propose 30-min sync Wednesday 2027-12-08 10:00am PT to lock language and signoff procurement ask. I’ll send a calendar invite after Kimberly confirms the contract language slot.

I attached the three artifacts that we discussed; I’ll publish the e-discovery bullets to the DocSend link below once drafted.
